abstract: Maintains ROV navigation, tooling depth ratings, and umbilical winch tare weights
system_message:
You are Subsea Robotics Lead (ROV). As the Subsea Robotics Lead (ROV), you oversee the technical readiness of subsea robotic assets, maintaining records for subsea acoustic tracking system activation, work-class ROV operational depth ratings, umbilical winch tare weights, and umbilical telemetry bandwidth across candidate offshore emergency restoration plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Telemetry link calibration（FIBER）
information_points.content:
ROV-FIBER-FU6：For the Dynamic positioning umbilical spooling plan, optoelectronic bench testing indicates sustained umbilical telemetry bandwidth of 40 Gbps across the main telemetry transmission lines.
ROV-FIBER-L99：For the Autonomous robotic trenching and splicing plan, optoelectronic bench testing logs show sustained umbilical telemetry bandwidth of 10 Gbps along the main transmission lines.
ROV-FIBER-DWH：For the Modular deck gantry grapple recovery plan, optoelectronic bench testing demonstrates sustained umbilical telemetry bandwidth of 25 Gbps along the main transmission lines.

information_points.title: Maintains ROV navigation, tooling depth ratings, and umbilical winch tare weights（SUBSEA）
information_points.content:
ROV-SUBSEA-KKH：For the Modular deck gantry grapple recovery plan, acoustic tracking system activation is confirmed enabled on the ultra-short baseline transceiver array, the primary work-class ROV holds an operational depth rating of 2500 m, and the subsea winch tare mass is 35 t.
ROV-SUBSEA-L0Y：For the Autonomous robotic trenching and splicing plan, acoustic tracking system activation is confirmed enabled via the ultra-short baseline transceiver array, the primary work-class ROV has a certified operational depth rating of 2000 m, and the subsea winch tare mass is 35 t.
ROV-SUBSEA-HV3：For the Dynamic positioning umbilical spooling plan, the ultra-short baseline transceiver array confirms acoustic tracking system activation is enabled, while the primary work-class ROV has a certified operational depth rating of 3000 m and the launch and recovery subsea winch tare mass is 55 t.
